name: Plan a pad fracturing program
summary: When a producer awards a multi-well pad, the fracturing operations group turns the producer's completion program and the approved treatment design into an executable plan: which fleet and crew, on which dates, with how much horsepower, sand, chemicals and fuel, how the equipment will sit on the lease and how the frac crew will hand over with wireline and water contractors. An account manager, an operations manager, operations coordinators, a design engineer, a field supervisor, a logistics coordinator and an HSE advisor all take part. The work is slow because the producer's dates move with drilling progress, weather and budgets, and every move ripples into sand orders, crew rotations and the next pad on the fleet's schedule.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian pressure pumping company with six to eight crewed frac fleets working multi-well pads in Alberta and northeast BC from district bases, with a Calgary engineering and sales office.
baseline.notes: Common practice of large WCSB pressure pumpers in 2019-2022: ERP, spreadsheets, email and phone, fracture modelling software and a data van acquisition system; no automated scheduling optimiser.

unit_of_work: one pad program (a multi-well pad of typically two to six horizontal wells)
trigger: A producer's completions engineer sends a pad program under a master service agreement, or a pad is awarded through a tender or pricing agreement.
end_state: An issued pad program with fleet, dates, equipment list, site layout, material and fuel orders placed and a mobilization plan handed to dispatch, or the pad deferred by the producer.

volume.seasonality: Highest from December to mid-March when frozen ground opens muskeg leases; low from late March to May during spring break-up road bans; moderate summer and fall. 2020 had several near-idle months.

evidence.note: Kept the organisation file's 6-18-26 pads a month. Check: STEP's four Canadian crews averaged about 244 operating days per crew in 2021 (src2 supports days, not pads); at about 10-12 operating days per pad a crew completes about two pads a month, so 7 crews give about 14-18 pads, more when single-well work is mixed in.

surge.cause: Winter completion peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Winter peak is general WCSB knowledge and matches the organisation file; multiplier is an estimate.
Intake and producer date negotiation, about 2 hours a pad plus relationship time; estimate.
Weekly fleet scheduling meetings and program approval across four managers; estimate.
Coordinators carry most of the planning hours; about 25 hours a pad including changes; estimate.
Design handover and proppant substitution decisions; design itself is a separate process; estimate.
Lease visit, layout and program review, including driving; estimate.
Sand supply confirmation for each pad; estimate. Not listed among the organisation file's roles for this process.
Site hazard review during the lease visit; estimate. Not listed among the organisation file's roles for this process.

systems.name: Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
Dispatch and crew scheduling board (scheduling module, whiteboards, spreadsheets)
ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)
Fracture and cement placement modelling software
HSE incident, hazard assessment and audit system
Rail carrier and sand supplier railcar tracking portals

resources.name: Crew pickup trucks and light vehicles
Crewed hydraulic fracturing fleet (pumps, blender, data van, sand and chemical units, treating iron)

steps.name: Receive pad program from producer
steps.description: The account manager receives the producer's pad program by email: surface location, well names, stage counts, target tonnage per stage, preferred fluid system and a target start window. The account manager checks it is under a current price agreement, logs the opportunity and forwards it to the fracturing operations manager.

error.defect_description: Stage count or target window copied wrongly from the producer's email

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Open the pad job file
steps.description: An operations coordinator creates the pad job number in the ERP and a job folder on the shared drive, saves the producer's program, well surveys and wellhead details, and adds the pad as a tentative block on the fleet schedule spreadsheet.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Assign fleet and tentative dates
steps.description: At the weekly scheduling meeting the operations manager compares the pad's target window with each fleet's current pad end date, planned maintenance and crew rotations, and the horsepower and pressure rating the design will need. The manager slots the pad on a fleet and records tentative rig-up and pumping dates.

error.defect_description: Fleet double-booked or maintenance window missed because the schedule spreadsheet was out of date

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Offer the slot to the producer
steps.description: The account manager phones or emails the producer's completions engineer with the proposed fleet and start date, explains any conflict with the requested window and records the reply or the request for another date.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Wait for producer to confirm the slot
steps.description: The producer checks the slot against drilling rig progress, facility tie-in dates and budget approval, and confirms, asks for another date, or defers the pad to a later quarter.

evidence.note: Producer delays and work moving between quarters are reported by STEP (src2); shares are estimates.

steps.name: Drive to the lease
steps.description: The field supervisor assigned to the pad drives from the district base or a nearby pad to the producer's lease, usually on a day off the pumping schedule or between shifts, using lease directions and the LSD location from the pad file.

evidence.note: Lease visits wait for the drilling rig to move off and for the supervisor's rotation; drive times reflect WCSB distances of 1-3 hours each way.

steps.name: Inspect lease and access
steps.description: On the lease the field supervisor paces out the pad size, checks the access road, ground conditions, overhead lines, wellhead and frac tree positions, water source and tank or pond locations, and where the wireline unit and sand storage can sit. Photos and measurements go into the job file.

error.defect_description: Lease too small or soft ground missed, found on rig-up day

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Review site hazards with HSE
steps.description: The HSE advisor reviews the producer's site safety requirements, H2S classification, emergency response plan, muster areas and nearest medical facility, often on the same visit, and notes controls the pre-job hazard assessment must carry.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 2 section 7: hazard assessment before work begins at a work site

evidence.note: Hazard assessment duty from OHS Code Part 2 (src11); timing is an estimate.

steps.name: Receive the approved treatment design
steps.description: The design engineer hands over the producer-approved pump schedule for the pad and walks the coordinator through stage totals, maximum expected treating pressure and rate, fluid system and any special products. If the design is not yet approved the coordinator waits for it.

evidence.note: Service company engineering builds program designs with the customer (src1); waits are estimates.

steps.name: Calculate material quantities
steps.description: The coordinator multiplies the per-stage design by stage count and wells to get tonnes of each proppant mesh, cubic metres of water and litres of each chemical, adds a contingency of about five to ten percent, and builds the material schedule by pumping day in the pad workbook.

error.defect_description: Wrong stage count or unit conversion in the material workbook

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Size horsepower and equipment list
steps.description: From design rate and treating pressure the coordinator calculates hydraulic horsepower, adds standby pumps, and lists pumps, blender, data van, sand storage, chemical units, treating iron and manifold, matching unit numbers from the fleet roster and maintenance status.

error.defect_description: A unit in the shop for repair listed as available

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Draft site layout, fuel plan and mobilization plan
steps.description: Using the lease notes the coordinator draws the equipment spotting layout, estimates diesel or dual-fuel consumption by pumping day and delivery frequency, and drafts the mobilization plan listing units, origin, target arrival and road restrictions known so far.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Approve the pad program
steps.description: The operations manager reviews the equipment list against design pressure and rate, the material schedule against stage counts, the fleet dates against the next pad, and the layout. The manager approves or sends specific corrections back to the coordinator.

control.basis: Company approval of the job plan before materials are ordered

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Enter the proppant requirement
steps.description: The coordinator enters tonnes by mesh and daily delivery requirement into the proppant planning sheet and ERP requisition, with the pad's location and first pumping date, so supply chain can reserve sand at the transload and book trucks.

error.defect_description: Mesh or tonnage keyed wrongly when copied from the pad workbook

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Confirm sand supply and hauling
steps.description: The proppant logistics coordinator checks transload inventory, railcars in transit and last-mile trucking capacity for the pad's dates and confirms supply, or reports a shortfall of a mesh size and proposes a substitute or split delivery.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Approve proppant substitution
steps.description: The design engineer reviews the proposed substitute mesh or source against the design and conductivity needs, reruns the affected stages if needed, and gets the producer's agreement by email before the change is accepted.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Place chemical and fuel orders
steps.description: The coordinator sends the chemical requirement by product and pumping day to the chemical blending plant, and the diesel and natural gas requirement to fuel supply and the dual-fuel group, with site delivery points from the layout.

error.defect_description: Chemical volumes not updated after a design change

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Hold interface meeting with producer and contractors
steps.description: The coordinator chairs a call with the producer's completions supervisor, the wireline contractor and the water transfer company to agree rig-up date, zipper sequence, plug and perforating handovers, water supply rates and who supplies cranes, matting and light towers.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Wait for producer to confirm final schedule
steps.description: The producer confirms the final well list, start date and site readiness date once drilling and wellhead installation are done, or announces a slip, a change to stage counts, or a deferral.

evidence.note: Client location delays and work moved between quarters (src2); shares are estimates.

steps.name: Re-sequence dates and orders after a slip
steps.description: The coordinator moves the pad on the fleet schedule, tells supply chain to shift sand, chemical and fuel deliveries, checks the knock-on effect on the next pad and crew rotation, and tells the producer the new firm date.

error.defect_description: A delivery not moved, so sand arrives at an empty lease or the wrong date

next.condition: clashes with another pad, fleet must be reassigned

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Distribute the pad program
steps.description: The coordinator issues the pad program package to crew scheduling, HSE for the pre-job hazard assessment, the field supervisor and treater, dispatch for mobilization, and the district for field ticket set-up.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Field supervisor reviews the program
steps.description: The field supervisor and treater read the program, design, layout and equipment list, and flag gaps such as iron rated below expected pressure, too few standby pumps or a layout that blocks sand trucks.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Hold pre-job planning call
steps.description: Two to three days before the move the coordinator holds a call with the field supervisor, producer's wellsite supervisor and wireline lead to confirm arrival time, lease readiness, first-well sequence and outstanding deliveries.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: File final program and close planning
steps.description: The coordinator saves the final revision of the program, layout and orders in the job folder, updates the fleet schedule to firm, and records planned rig-up date for the district and billing set-up.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

exceptions.name: Producer slips the start date
exceptions.description: Drilling delays, wellhead availability or budget holds move the pad; dates, orders and the next pad on the fleet are re-sequenced, sometimes more than once.

exceptions.name: Fleet reassignment
exceptions.description: The producer's preferred dates clash with another pad and the manager moves the pad to a different fleet.

exceptions.name: Proppant mesh shortfall
exceptions.description: The transload is short of a mesh size and the design engineer and producer approve a substitute.

exceptions.name: Design change after planning
exceptions.description: The producer changes stage counts or tonnage; quantities and orders are recalculated from the new design.

exceptions.name: Pad deferred
exceptions.description: The producer defers the pad to a later quarter or cancels it.

benchmarks.unit: days from pad program received to firm program issued

evidence.note: Estimate: producers typically give two to six weeks' notice of a pad and confirm the final date within a week of rig-up.

benchmarks.metric: fracturing operating days per crew per year
benchmarks.population: STEP Energy Services Canadian fracturing, 2021 (977 days, 4 crews)

evidence.note: 977 operating days with four crews in 2021 (src2); used to size pads per fleet-month.

pain_points.description: Producer date changes ripple into sand, chemical and fuel orders and into the next pad on the fleet; coordinators re-plan by hand in spreadsheets.

evidence.note: Client delays and work moving between quarters reported by STEP (src2); manual re-planning is an estimate.

pain_points.description: Material quantities are re-keyed from the design into the pad workbook and then into ERP requisitions, so a design change can leave an order stale.

evidence.note: Typical 2019-2022 practice of spreadsheets beside the ERP.

pain_points.description: Lease visits wait for the drilling rig to leave and the field supervisor to be off pumping duty.

evidence.note: Estimate from field rotation patterns.

sources.title: Trican - Hydraulic fracturing
sources.supports: Engineering team works with customers on program design, MiniFrac analysis, pore and closure pressure; fracture design combines fracture models with geological and geophysical data and formation frac databases; slickwater, HVFR, crosslinked, foam and other fluid systems; full-service lab in Calgary; logistical planning for chemicals, proppants, people and equipment; Tier 4 dynamic gas blending pumps.

sources.title: STEP Energy Services Ltd. Reports Fourth Quarter and Year End 2021 Results
sources.supports: Canadian fracturing: 977 operating days in 2021 and 704 in 2020 with 4 and 3 crews; 1,012,000 tonnes of proppant in 2021; weather delays in late December 2021 and extreme cold in January 2022; extended delays on a client location from well conditions; work moved between quarters; spring break-up conditions restrict operations; smaller jobs and single-well work less efficient than multi-well pads.

sources.title: Occupational Health and Safety Code (legislation search)
sources.supports: OHS Code Part 2 Hazard Assessment, Elimination and Control, section 7 Hazard assessment and section 8 Worker participation.

assumptions: Loaded hourly costs are taken from the organisation file (wage plus about 30-35 percent benefits and overhead as stated there).
One case is one pad. Small single-well jobs in the same calendar would follow a shorter path; they are folded into the low end of step times.
Detailed fracture design is a separate process (te-frac-treatment-design); this workflow starts its material planning once that design is approved and loops back when it changes.
The logistics coordinator, field supervisor and HSE advisor are organisation file roles that the process_map entry does not list; they take part here.

Simulated median cycle time of about 25 days against a 21-day estimate comes from repeated slip and re-sequence loops; it is dominated by waiting on the producer and the calendar. Hands-on time is about 35 hours per pad including rework.
